summary: This work proposes a high-frequency transmon architecture operating at $12$ GHz (spanning $11$–$13.5$ GHz) designed to achieve longer coherence times and higher scalability than conventional $4$–$6$ GHz qubits. The design targets an 8-qubit prototype with pathways to $72$ qubits, aiming for $T_1 \approx 1.9$ ms and quality factors $Q \approx 2.75 \times 10^7$ using tantalum and Nb/Al/AlO$_x$ trilayer junctions on high-resistivity Si.
motivation: Higher operating frequencies enable faster gate times and smaller device footprints while maintaining coherence, potentially improving scalability and operation at elevated temperatures relative to standard $5$ GHz transmons.
method: A new transmon topology is designed with optimized superconducting junctions (Ta and Nb/Al/AlO$_x$ tri-layers on high-resistivity silicon) to operate stably at $12$ GHz with reduced charge noise.
result: Preliminary design targets relaxation times of $1.9$ ms and quality factors of $2.75 \times 10^7$, with pathways to scale from 8 to 72 qubits per chip.
